description: Cross-implementation vectors for the ReceiptV1 envelope and the section 5.3 stage rules of draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 (sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.6). Every expected acceptance, rejection and state is fixed in the generator from the draft text or from RFC 3339, cited per case in its derivation, and the generator exits without writing this file if the TypeScript reference disagrees with one of them. sdk_failure_codes and sdk_errors are this SDK pair own vocabulary, which the draft does not name: the draft fixes the state, not the code string, and the Python port sharing these strings is SDK parity rather than a protocol claim. A case whose signed flag is true carries a receipt_id and a signature value that are the output of the TypeScript reference issuer over that exact body, so they are bytes another implementation must reproduce. A case whose flag is false carries either an all-zero placeholder, because the record is one the issuer refuses to mint at all, or a signature that no longer covers the body because the case edits a member the issuer owns; either way the structural rule under test runs before any signature is examined, which is what makes those cases sound. This file is not "TS verified" and no case in it should be described that way.

provenance_definitions.draft-derived: the expected acceptance, rejection or state follows from the draft text, with RFC 3339 where cited; TypeScript output was not consulted to decide it.
provenance_definitions.ruling-derived: the draft names the case but does not fix its outcome, and the expected outcome comes from a ruling recorded by the principal for this programme. The case derivation says which question it answers. These are the cases a later revision of the draft would have to state in normative text for the expectation to become draft-derived.

keys.note: Deterministic test keys. The private keys are the byte patterns below, which are test values and never key material for anything real.

conventions.envelope: run the envelope validator over receipt in its full form, values included, and compare acceptance with expected.accepts. An unsigned fixture carries an all-zero receipt_id and an all-zero signature value, both of which satisfy the hexadecimal forms, so the case turns on the member under test.
conventions.stage: run the stage validator over receipt with the context expected_receipt_type and boundary_identity when they are not null, and compare status, stage, boundary_identity and the failure code set.
conventions.verify: run the receipt verifier with a key resolver of the named kind: correct returns the public key for the signer, none returns nothing, raises throws, other_key returns the unrelated public key. Compare status, signer_authority and the error set.

withheld: delegation_ref for an authority basis with no delegation: section 5.1 line 983 names the case and section 5 gives it no encoding anywhere. Only the "sha256:" form of a delegation_id is exercised here, and the binding of that value to a leaf is the section 5.6 composition point, which needs a chain and is not a single-record rule.

Recomputation of action_ref from an independently supplied action, recomputation of decision_ref from its components, and resolution of prev against the record it names: all three are section 5.6 composition points rather than stage rules, and a single-record vector cannot carry the second artifact.
The approval obligations of lines 1093 to 1099, which are enforcement-boundary state: expiry, atomic consumption of receipt_id, rechecking time and revocation, and completing the spend reservation.
Evidence resolution under section 5.5, implemented nowhere in either SDK.

cases.title: A conforming action-intent record is accepted

derivation.note: The control. Every rejection below is a one-member change from this record, so a rejection is the rule firing and not a broken fixture.

cases.title: action_ref as a one-element array

derivation.note: action_ref is the aps-action-ref-v2 digest, a string. A malformed artifact gets a defined result and is not coerced into a conforming one.

cases.title: receipt_id as a one-element array

derivation.note: receipt_id is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, a string.

cases.title: issuer as a number

derivation.note: issuer is the party responsible for the record, a string identifier.

cases.title: subject_agent as an object

derivation.note: subject_agent is the acting agent, a string identifier.

cases.title: receipt_type as a number

derivation.note: receipt_type identifies a stage defined in section 5.3, a string.

cases.title: delegation_ref as a bare 64 hex digest

derivation.note: delegation_ref identifies the selected AuthorityDelegationV1 leaf; the envelope example writes it with the "sha256:" prefix and section 3.1 gives delegation_id that exact form.

cases.title: delegation_ref with uppercase hexadecimal

derivation.note: The digest is lowercase hexadecimal.

cases.title: delegation_ref as an identifier that is not a digest

derivation.note: The authority-basis case of line 983 has no encoding anywhere in section 5, so the only form this validator can check is the one the envelope example states. Recorded as a question, not as an accepted alternative.

cases.title: evidence_refs sha256 as a one-element array

derivation.note: sha256 is the lowercase hexadecimal digest of the artifact bytes, a string.

cases.title: evidence_refs artifact_type as a number

derivation.note: An evidence reference contains exactly artifact_type and sha256, and artifact_type names the rules that select the bytes.

cases.title: decision_ref as a one-element array

derivation.note: decision_ref is a 64 lowercase hexadecimal digest, a string. It is conditional on the stage, so it is exercised on a record that carries it.

cases.title: prev as a one-element array

derivation.note: prev is the receipt_id of another record, a string. Same reason for using a record that carries it.

cases.title: a signature value as a one-element array

derivation.note: A signature value is 128 lowercase hexadecimal characters, a string. The one-element array of that string coerced through the pattern test.

cases.title: evidence_refs out of order

derivation.note: References are sorted first by the UTF-8 bytes of artifact_type and then by the ASCII bytes of sha256.

cases.title: A duplicate evidence reference

derivation.note: evidence_refs is duplicate-free.

cases.title: An unknown envelope member

derivation.note: A ReceiptV1 is a closed JSON object.

cases.title: A not-applicable member present as null

derivation.note: A member that is not applicable is absent, not null.

cases.title: A conforming leap second in issued_at

derivation.note: RFC 3339 admits time-second 60 for a leap second and writes it YYYY-MM-DDT23:59:60Z. No leap-second table is consulted; the hour, minute and day settle it.

cases.title: Second 60 that is not on the last day of a month

derivation.note: Every second-60 value outside 23:59 on the last day of its month is invalid.

cases.title: Second 60 that is not at 23:59

derivation.note: Same rule, failing on the hour.

cases.title: February 29 outside a leap year

derivation.note: The timestamp must be a calendar instant, checked in the proleptic Gregorian calendar.

cases.title: A Unicode noncharacter in a string value

derivation.note: A verifier parses bounded I-JSON. The same reading of I-JSON is applied on the section 4.1 and section 3 surfaces of these SDKs.

cases.title: A Unicode noncharacter in an object key

derivation.note: The rule covers member names as well as values.

cases.title: An unpaired surrogate in a string

derivation.note: A string containing an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate has no UTF-8 encoding and is rejected rather than repaired.

cases.title: A conforming action intent

derivation.note: The control for the intent stage.

cases.title: An action intent issued by someone other than the acting agent

derivation.note: issuer and subject_agent MUST be the acting agent.

cases.title: An action intent carrying prev

derivation.note: prev MUST be absent from an action-intent record.

cases.title: An action intent carrying decision_ref

derivation.note: decision_ref MUST be absent from an action-intent record.

cases.title: An action intent whose result status is not declared

derivation.note: result MUST contain exactly profile aps-action-intent-result-v1 and status declared.

cases.title: An action intent whose result carries an extra member

derivation.note: Exactly those two members: the result is the closed typed object defined by receipt_type.

cases.title: An action intent under another result profile

derivation.note: A wrong result profile for a stage that is recognised is invalid, not unsupported: that result object is closed.

cases.title: A conforming policy decision with the boundary identity supplied

derivation.note: The control for the decision stage.

cases.title: The same decision with no boundary identity supplied

derivation.note: The expected boundary identity is verifier trust input. Unestablished is indeterminate and never valid, and a caller may not collapse it into valid.

cases.title: A decision whose issuer is not the supplied boundary

derivation.note: A mismatch against a supplied identity is invalid.

cases.title: A decision whose issuer equals its subject_agent

derivation.note: The draft states no rule that issuer differs from subject_agent for this stage. None is invented: the record stands or falls on the supplied boundary identity.

cases.title: A decision with no prev

derivation.note: prev is REQUIRED for a policy-decision record and is the receipt_id of the action-intent record.

cases.title: A decision with no decision_ref

derivation.note: decision_ref is REQUIRED for a policy-decision record.

cases.title: A verdict outside the three the draft names

derivation.note: verdict is permit, deny, or narrow.

cases.title: A permit with a null effective_authority_ref

derivation.note: effective_authority_ref is null for deny and a digest for permit or narrow.

cases.title: A permit with a null valid_until

derivation.note: valid_until is null for deny and a timestamp later than issued_at for permit or narrow.

cases.title: A conforming deny decision

derivation.note: A deny decision carries both nulls by rule. It is a conforming record, not a temporal failure.

cases.title: A deny decision that still carries an effective_authority_ref

derivation.note: Null for deny is a rule in both directions.

cases.title: valid_until equal to issued_at

derivation.note: Later than issued_at is strict, and the comparison is against this record own issuance time.

cases.title: Constraints not sorted by UTF-8 bytes

derivation.note: constraints is a duplicate-free array of NFC strings sorted by UTF-8 bytes. A verifier accepts the canonical form and does not normalize an untrusted wire object.

cases.title: A duplicate constraint

derivation.note: Duplicate-free.

cases.title: A constraint that is not in NFC

derivation.note: The decomposed form of the same character is not the NFC form.

cases.title: Canonical constraints are accepted

derivation.note: The control for the three rejections above.

cases.title: A decision result under another profile

derivation.note: A wrong result profile for a recognised stage is invalid, where an unknown envelope profile is unsupported.

cases.title: A conforming succeeded action result

derivation.note: The control for the result stage.

cases.title: succeeded with no effect_ref

derivation.note: For succeeded, effect_ref is REQUIRED.

cases.title: succeeded carrying an error_code

derivation.note: For succeeded, error_code is null.

cases.title: A conforming failed result with no effect artifact

derivation.note: For failed, effect_ref is either a digest of a returned error artifact or null.

cases.title: A conforming failed result with an error artifact digest

derivation.note: The other admitted pairing for failed.

cases.title: failed with an empty error_code

derivation.note: For failed, error_code is a non-empty stable identifier. Stability is not machine-checkable and is not claimed.

cases.title: A conforming unknown result

derivation.note: For unknown, both are null.

cases.title: unknown carrying an effect_ref

derivation.note: Both null means both.

cases.title: A status outside the three the draft names

derivation.note: status is succeeded, failed, or unknown.

cases.title: An action result missing a result member

derivation.note: result contains exactly profile, status, effect_ref and error_code.

cases.title: effect_ref as a one-element array

derivation.note: A non-null effect_ref is a lowercase hexadecimal digest, a string.

cases.title: An action result under another result profile

derivation.note: profile is aps-action-result-v1.

cases.title: An action result with no prev and no decision_ref

derivation.note: Both are REQUIRED for an action-result record.

cases.title: A receipt_type outside section 5.3

derivation.note: receipt_type identifies a stage defined in section 5.3. A value outside those three is unsupported and never valid, and its body is not judged against a stage schema it may not belong to. Section 5.1 does not state this case, so it is recorded as ruled rather than as draft text.

cases.title: Another envelope profile

derivation.note: An unknown required profile is unsupported.

cases.title: A malformed envelope with a known stage type

derivation.note: The closed envelope check runs before the stage rules, and a structural failure is invalid whatever the receipt_type says.

cases.title: The caller expects a stage the record does not name

derivation.note: The stage comes from the record. A caller-supplied expectation that disagrees with receipt_type is itself a failure, not a way to select the rules.

cases.title: A resolvable key and a good signature

derivation.note: The control.

cases.title: The resolver returns no key

derivation.note: Key resolution is its own outcome and missing live state is indeterminate. An unresolved key is not evidence that a signature is wrong.

cases.title: The resolver raises

derivation.note: A failing resolver is a resolution outcome, and a verification interface handles it through a defined result.

cases.title: A resolvable key that did not sign this receipt

derivation.note: A resolved key whose signature does not verify is an invalid cryptographic check.

cases.title: Another envelope profile

derivation.note: Unsupported is its own answer and is not collapsed into invalid or into valid.

cases.title: The resolver names: subject or key not found

derivation.note: Section 2.5 requires a resolver to keep six outcomes apart. The draft does not map each to a verification state, so the mapping here comes from a recorded ruling: not found is indeterminate, under its own reason.

cases.title: The resolver names: ambiguous, including duplicate key identifiers

derivation.note: A key set in which a key identifier is duplicated is malformed for the set as a whole. Ruled indeterminate, under its own reason.

cases.title: The resolver names: transport unreachability

derivation.note: Ruled indeterminate. A deployment MAY adopt a fail-open policy for transport unreachability only, and a degraded outcome is still not a positive verification.

cases.title: The resolver names: structurally malformed key material

derivation.note: Malformed material that loads but is wrong fails closed even under a fail-open policy, and is never a signature failure: no signature check ran.

cases.title: The resolver names: an unsupported identifier scheme

derivation.note: The one outcome of the six that is unsupported rather than indeterminate, which is what line 1226 says of an unknown required profile and is how the ruling maps it.

cases.title: Key material that is not a 32-byte Ed25519 key

derivation.note: The resolver named no outcome; the material it returned is 16 bytes. It must not reach the signature check, which returns false on a length mismatch and would report a failed signature for bytes nothing checked.

cases.title: A signature from another signer that does not verify

derivation.note: Line 999 requires one signature from issuer and line 1041 has a verifier verify every REQUIRED signature. Signatures sit outside receipt_id, so a third party can append one to a published receipt without changing a digest. Ruled: a failure outside the required set does not change the aggregate state and is reported on its own axis.

cases.title: A second signature from the issuer that does not verify

derivation.note: The same append from the issuer, who is in the required set, does decide. The pair with RC-V12 is what shows the axis is the required set and not the count.

cases.title: A verifier requires a signer the receipt does not carry

derivation.note: The required set is the issuer plus what the applicable profile or the verifier requires. A named signer carrying no descriptor at all is a missing required signature.
